title.narrative: Improved Technical and Vocational Education and Training for Employment Project

description.narrative: The project will assist the government in implementing reforms to strengthen the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) system and to prepare students to be more competitive and responsive to employment and industry demands. It will focus on construction trades and agriculture programs in 10 TVET colleges identified by the government as centers of excellence, which will serve as models for subsequent reforms to other TVET colleges in the country.

Output: TVET college governance and management strengthened Indicator: All project TVET colleges complied with annual audited financial and performance reporting requirements in line with the Governance Manual Progress/Status: Governance Manual to be updated pending updating of the DHERST Governance Manual.
Started initial steps toward enhancing TVET college governance and financial management through the introduction of computerized accounting systems by having preliminary discussions with DHERST on budgeting and financial reporting requirements for colleges. These requirements will be consolidated with feedback from the detailed Financial Management Assessment Questionnaire (FMAQ), developed in late 2024 to assess existing capacities across colleges to tailor support and inform the implementation roadmap. Simultaneously, training needs are being identified to ensure staff are prepared for the transition to computerized systems, with theoretical and on-the-job training phases scheduled in the upcoming quarters.
Further supporting this transition, the Project has commenced review of the comprehensive Financial Management Manual and Guidebook for the PMU developed in 2024. This resource covers key areas such as budgeting, fund management, accounting, and audit processes, complete with templates and annexes. Once vetted by key stakeholders (DHERST, GoPNG, ADB, DFAT), it will serve as a foundational reference for both PMU and college-level financial operations. Data Source: Quarterly and annual progress reports by the PMU, quarterly report by the TST, and project completion report by the project evaluation consulting firm Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y
